purpose: Fenofibric acid is used to help lower high triglycerides (a type of fat in your blood) and raise your good cholesterol (HDL). It can also lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in some cases. It is often used along with diet changes and sometimes with a statin medication to improve your overall cholesterol levels.
how_it_works: This medication works by activating a natural protein in your body that helps control how fats are made and broken down. It tells your liver to produce fewer triglycerides and helps your body clear them from the blood faster. Think of it like turning down the factory that makes too much fat in your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, back pain, nausea, runny or stuffy nose, and upset stomach. Some people may notice mild muscle aches or joint pain. These are usually mild but let your doctor know if anything bothers you.
warnings: Rarely, this medication can cause serious muscle breakdown (called rhabdomyolysis), especially if taken with a statin — watch for unusual muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine and call your doctor right away. It may affect your liver, so your doctor may check liver blood tests periodically. Avoid this medication if you have severe kidney or liver disease, or a gallbladder condition. Tell your doctor about all your medications because fenofibric acid can interact with blood thinners like warfarin.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 35 mg to 105 mg taken by mouth once daily, with or without food. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and other medications. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or chew it.
